key_insight: OmniShotCut reconceptualizes shot-boundary detection as a structured relational prediction problem and uses a Shot-Query Transformer to jointly reason about shot relationships and boundaries, producing more interpretable and sensitive boundary detections.
problem_solved: Addresses unreliable, non-interpretable shot boundaries, missed subtle discontinuities, and limitations of noisy/low-diversity annotations and outdated benchmarks in existing SBD methods.
method: Formulate SBD as structured relational prediction that jointly estimates shot boundaries and inter-shot relations instead of independent frame-wise decisions.
Introduce a Shot-Query Transformer that uses explicit shot queries and cross-attention over temporal features to capture holistic relational context across frames.
Refine training/evaluation practices to mitigate noisy labels and benchmark gaps (improving annotation diversity and evaluation fidelity).
impact: Provides practitioners with a more robust, interpretable SBD model that better detects subtle discontinuities and supports downstream video tasks (editing, indexing, summarization); updated evaluation practices help accelerate fair comparisons and progress.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram: Shot-Query Transformer showing shot queries, cross-attention to frame features, and joint boundary/relationship outputs.
Timeline visualization: example video timeline with ground-truth vs. OmniShotCut-detected boundaries and confidence/interpretability cues.
Relational graph: nodes = shots, edges = predicted inter-shot relations highlighting where structural cues drive boundary decisions.
Comparison chart: precision/recall (or F1) bars vs. prior SOTA and a small table noting improvements on noisy/subtle transitions.
paper_title: OmniShotCut: Holistic Relational Shot Boundary Detection with Shot-Query Transformer
paper_authors: Boyang Wang, Guangyi Xu, Zhipeng Tang, Jiahui Zhang, Zezhou Cheng
